summary: Space Miners transforms static planetary mission catalogs into a fully developed, zero-install 3D deep-space archive. To make decades of off-world engineering heritage accessible to students, educators, and the public, our web application renders interactive 3D globes of the Moon and Mars in Three.js, plotted with real NASA latitude-longitude beacons. Selecting a beacon triggers a smooth GSAP camera zoom-morph from deep space into planetary orbit and opens a dedicated hardware telemetry view. We cataloged eight historic Lunar and Martian artifacts—Apollo 11 Descent Stage, Apollo 15 Lunar Rover, Surveyor 3, Ranger 4, Ingenuity Helicopter, Opportunity, Sojourner, and InSight—pairing each with a custom drag-to-rotate 3D procedural hardware hologram, mission backstory, scientific breakthroughs, current environmental condition, an interactive STEM quiz, and official NASA/NSSDC documentation. Our project shows that retired spacecraft aren't dead debris, but priceless archaeological monuments and active scientific testbeds—from Apollo 11’s passive laser mirrors still operating today to Ingenuity’s 20-year Martian weather station.
details:
1. EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW: WHAT SPACE MINERS DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Space Miners ("Abandoned But Not Forgotten") is a fully functional, interactive 3D planetary archive and STEM education platform. Over the past six decades, humanity has left landers, rovers, helicopters, and impact probes across the Moon and Mars. Yet public records of this hardware typically exist as fragmented, static tables of coordinates and masses. Space Miners turns those records into an explorable 3D mission control experience:

• 3D Orbital Command Interface (index.html & script.js):

  - Renders interactive 3D spheres of the Moon and Mars inside a 4,500-star WebGL scene with solar and rim lighting, orbital rings, and procedurally generated HTML5 Canvas surface and bump maps.

  - Uses spherical trigonometry (latLonToVector3) to convert official NASA landing/impact latitude and longitude coordinates into exact 3D Cartesian surface beacons.

  - Employs GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform) and Three.js OrbitControls for seamless camera zoom-morph transitions across three states: Deep Space Overview -> Planetary Orbit HUD -> Surface Beacon Telemetry Preview.

• Data-Driven Telemetry & 3D Hardware Hologram Engine (equipment.html):

  - A single modular template dynamically renders all 8 artifacts via URL query parameters with an instant top switcher bar.

  - Generates interactive, drag-to-rotate 3D procedural spacecraft holograms on a cyan holographic grid—modeling the octagonal Apollo Descent Stage, 6-wheeled planetary rovers, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (with counter-rotating animated coaxial blades), and tripod/solar-wing geophysical landers.

  - Presents four structured narrative layers per artifact: (1) Mission Story: Why Was It Left Behind?, (2) The Science It Made Possible, (3) What Is Its Condition Today?, and (4) an interactive Space Explorer Challenge Quiz with instant grading, plus a direct outbound link to primary NASA/NSSDC documentation.

2. ARCHIVE INVENTORY (4 LUNAR + 4 MARTIAN SITES)

• Lunar Artifacts (The Moon):

  1. Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage ("Eagle") — Sea of Tranquility 

  2. Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle ("Moon Buggy") — Hadley–Apennine 

  3. Surveyor 3 Robotic Lander — Ocean of Storms 

  4. Ranger 4 Lunar Impact Probe — Lunar Far Side 

• Martian Artifacts (Mars):

  5. Ingenuity Mars Helicopter ("Ginny") — Jezero Crater / Valinor Hills 

  6. Opportunity Mars Exploration Rover (MER-B) — Perseverance Valley 

  7. Sojourner Rover & Pathfinder Lander — Ares Vallis 

  8. InSight Mars Geophysical Lander — Elysium Planitia 

3. CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED

• IMPACT:

  Space Miners bridges the gap between raw planetary databases and public/classroom STEM literacy. By reframing "abandoned" hardware as living scientific instruments and engineering monuments, users discover that Apollo 11's passive Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector still works today without electricity (proving the Moon drifts 3.8 cm/year), Surveyor 3 gave humanity its only physical study of multi-year lunar radiation exposure when Apollo 12 astronauts retrieved its camera, and Ingenuity still operates as a 20-year stationary Martian weather station after completing 72 flights.

• CREATIVITY:

  Instead of relying on multi-megabyte external 3D model files (.gltf/.obj) or giant image textures that stall on school Wi-Fi, we engineered a 100% procedural 3D pipeline in Vanilla JavaScript and Three.js. Both planetary crater/regolith bump maps and 3D spacecraft holograms (gold Kapton foil, solar panels, rocker-bogie wheels, and coaxial rotors) are synthesized algorithmically at runtime in milliseconds.

• VALIDITY:

  Every coordinate transformation uses real spherical-to-Cartesian mathematics, and all telemetry figures (mass, coordinates, mission dates, and material degradation from UV radiation, micrometeorites, and Martian dust storms) are grounded in aerospace physics. The web app is fully developed, responsive across desktop and mobile devices, requires zero installation or build steps, and is live today for classrooms worldwide.

• RELEVANCE:

  NASA data is the backbone of the application. Coordinates drive the 3D beacon placement on the globes, engineering specifications drive the procedural hologram archetypes, and mission outcomes drive the interactive quizzes. Every artifact record links directly to its authoritative NASA Mission Page or NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDC) record.

• PRESENTATION:

  Designed with a glassmorphic orbital telemetry aesthetic (cyan for Lunar, amber-red for Martian), the interface guides users effortlessly from macro planetary exploration to micro hardware inspection, culminating in a self-testing quiz that reinforces learning.

4. TECHNOLOGY STACK & TOOLS USED

• Frontend Structure & Styling: HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap 5.3.3, Google Fonts 

• 3D Rendering & Interaction: Three.js (r128), Three.js OrbitControls, HTML5 2D Canvas API

• Animation & State Transitions: GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform 3.12.2), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+)

• Deployment & Version Control: Git, GitHub, and GitHub Pages (https://jzaman2004.github.io/Space-Miners/)

5. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

In full compliance with 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge rules, Team Space Miners discloses that Super Intelligence (LLM coding tools) was used to assist in structuring procedural Three.js geometry code. All NASA mission facts, coordinates, masses, and source URLs were verified against official NASA documentation. No NASA logos, insignia, or branding elements were generated or modified using SI tools.
